name: SDB
tagline: Tiny embeddable C string key-value database from the radare2 project, built on djb's cdb format.
description: SDB is a small string key-value database written in C by pancake (Sergi Alvarez) and maintained by the radare2 organisation, where it stores the metadata radare2 accumulates while analysing binaries. Data lives in memory and is synced atomically to a compact variant of D. J. Bernstein's cdb on-disk hash format, so a database file is never left half-written. On top of plain keys it adds namespaces, array syntax, JSON path get/set, numeric increment and decrement, glob-based deletes and a command-line shell; a companion mcsdbd daemon serves the data over the memcached protocol, and it compiles with Emscripten for JavaScript. It is MIT-licensed and actively maintained, with 2.5.x releases in 2026.

scale.notes: Single-process library; whole databases are rewritten on sync, so it suits small to medium datasets.

strengths: Very small, dependency-free C library that is easy to vendor
Atomic sync to cdb files means the on-disk database is never corrupted
Namespaces, arrays and JSON-path access on plain string keys
Battle-tested as radare2's internal metadata store
Permissive MIT license and active maintenance
weaknesses: Values are strings; no typed data, secondary indexes or queries
Sync rewrites the cdb file, which gets slow for large databases
Single-process: no concurrent writers or networking beyond the memcached shim
useCases: Embedded configuration and metadata storage in C programs
Storing analysis state in reverse-engineering tools
Lightweight persistent caches with a memcached front end
